End-to-end testing confirmed successful email delivery, response capture, task completion, and correct Approved or Rejected routing in the test environment.

The diagnostic process was then prepared and shared for UAT validation together with detailed import, configuration, execution, and evidence-collection instructions. The activity is completed, with the next step pending client testing in UAT to determine whether the issue is environment-specific and requires Product escalation.

data.MSHP_TaskLogDesc:
Completed a full post-optimization performance assessment of Fidelity Bank’s ProcessMaker PROD environment and consolidated the findings into a formal client-facing Production Environment Performance Validation Report. The analysis was based on controlled Chrome DevTools network traces and ProcessMaker Server-Timing measurements collected across the main production user journeys.

Reviewed and documented performance across Inbox, Tasks, Cases, Processes, Designer, Administration, authentication, and case-detail operations. The assessment confirmed that all representative normal or warm core requests completed within 1.50 seconds or less, with no core HTTP 4xx&#x2F;5xx errors observed during the validated business journeys. Key results included a 778 ms median Inbox task-list response, 439 ms Admin Users response, 432 ms case-detail task lookup, and 867 ms task-data response.

Performed deeper analysis of the initial Process-list outlier, confirming that the first request reached 11.84 seconds but recovered immediately to 1.25–1.36 seconds on subsequent runs, representing approximately an 89% recovery and indicating transient cold&#x2F;backend behavior rather than persistent degradation.

Analyzed Server-Timing data to separate browser, application boot, provider, controller, and database contributions. Identified the remaining targeted optimization opportunities around authentication variability, case-counter database cost, duplicate frontend requests, and the Process Bookmarks timeout, while confirming that these findings do not indicate broad PROD instability.

Prepared the final 12-page report with an executive summary, validation methodology, consolidated results, detailed performance evidence, technical interpretation, residual risk register, prioritized recommendations, follow-up validation plan, management summary, and appendices containing the detailed measurement register and duplicate-request evidence.

The final assessment concludes that Fidelity Bank’s PROD environment demonstrates materially improved and stable performance across the validated core workflows and is suitable for continued normal use, with the remaining observations documented as focused follow-up items rather than system-wide performance issues.

MSHP_AllActiveProjWithTasks.MSHP_ExecutiveSummary: A thorough post-optimization performance assessment was conducted, with a full analysis of key processes to provide in-depth performance insights. The key performance validation results confirmed operations within acceptable timeframes and identified optimization opportunities. A professional detailed report was prepared, comprising a comprehensive executive summary of findings, recommendations, and next steps.

data.MSHP_TaskLogDesc: Weekly Calls

Completed a follow-up review and correction of the Offboarding email notification after the client removed the checkbox column from the Line Manager form. The issue was traced to the email template still depending on the removed checkbox value to determine which business-system rows should be displayed, which caused the business-system information to stop populating correctly.

The email mapping was updated to use the remaining business-system fields and to exclude rows where the related transfer information is blank. The original two-column Line Manager form design was preserved, and the email was also adjusted so uploaded documents are no longer attached or displayed, in line with the updated client requirement.

A fully populated test case was executed using the applicable Yes selections to verify that the expected questions, answers, business-system information, arrays, and conditional values render correctly in the final email. The fix has been completed and successfully tested.

Completed the initial configuration and data-model design for the Snap Send Solve dynamic questionnaire solution in ProcessMaker. Three related Collections were created to support the configuration structure: SSS Request Configurations, SSS Question Assignments, and SSS Question Options. These Collections were designed to determine which questions should be displayed based on the selected Request Type, Request Category, and Subcategory.

The relationships between the Collections were also defined using stable configuration and assignment keys so questions can be reused across different request configurations while preserving their own mandatory status, display order, render type, validation behavior, and selectable options. The structure was prepared to support the exact values expected by OneCouncil and future synchronization by KPMG.

The configuration framework is now in place and ready for final refinement once the remaining TechnologyOne&#x2F;OneCouncil source fields and question-option relationships are confirmed.

Advanced the development of the Offboarding email template and completed the mapping of the Line Manager screen data into the email output. The template was configured to render the submitted questions and answers, including complex conditional sections such as Teams extensions, call queues, CC4 call centre queues, Check Groups, and the Business Systems Loop. Selected business systems and their related information were formatted into a readable structure suitable for downstream email processing.

The email structure was also reviewed for compatibility with the client’s Helpdesk system and Classic Outlook limitations. A test email was sent to the Helpdesk test address to validate how the HTML content is rendered after ingestion. The main template development and screen-data mapping are nearly complete, with final Helpdesk validation and the separate post-submit data sanitization enhancement remaining.

data.MSHP_Project: Banco de Tierra del Fuego - Managed Services 2.0

data.MSHP_TaskLogDesc:
Completed an extensive investigation into the HTTP 500 errors affecting a subset of user profiles during the global date-format update. The analysis included reviewing automation execution metrics, comparing successful and failing users, reproducing the issue manually through the native ProcessMaker User Administration screen, inspecting requests and responses with browser DevTools, and testing direct PUT &#x2F;users&#x2F;{id} calls using the documented API structure.

The investigation confirmed that the problem was not caused by the date format itself or by the automation, as the same affected users could not initially be saved through the native interface or API. Further comparison identified a strong relationship with older&#x2F;legacy user records and the recommendations information stored within the user meta structure, which appeared to create an incompatible data structure during profile updates. The remaining users were subsequently processed successfully after isolating the problematic condition.

All technical evidence, reproduction steps, API behavior, affected-user patterns, DevTools findings, and the legacy meta&#x2F;recommendations observation were consolidated for escalation. The issue was documented and escalated to CloudOps for backend-level review and confirmation of the underlying platform&#x2F;data inconsistency.
data.MSHP_TaskProjectName: Banco de Tierra del Fuego - Managed Services 2.0

data.MSHP_TaskLogDesc:
Completed the design, implementation, and validation of a new ProcessMaker 4 process to centrally manage the user date format and avoid the need to update user profiles one by one.

The process was structured with two independent paths. The first is a manual diagnostic and application flow, allowing an administrator to run a safe DRY_RUN, review which users are already compliant, identify which accounts require changes, and then either apply the format immediately or finish without making any updates. The second is an automated reconciliation flow triggered by a daily timer, which checks the current user configuration and applies the required format when needed.

Configured the target format as d&#x2F;m&#x2F;Y H:i to represent DD&#x2F;MM&#x2F;YYYY HH:mm. The diagnostic path was implemented to scan all users through the ProcessMaker API without modifying any records, while generating detailed execution metrics such as scanned users, compliant users, candidates, users that would be updated, failures, API calls, retries, duration, and execution ID.

Implemented the ENFORCE logic to update only users that do not currently match the required format. Before each update, the script re-reads the user to avoid stale changes, preserves the required user data in the PUT payload, applies the new datetime_format, and performs an additional API call afterward to verify that the value was actually persisted. Successfully updated users are recorded as updated_and_verified.

Added handling for concurrent changes so that users already corrected by another action during execution are treated as compliant rather than as failures. Added runtime limits, pagination safeguards, HTTP retries, transport error handling, error sampling, pending-user tracking, and fatal error reporting.

Built dedicated result screens for both the diagnostic and final normalization stages. The diagnostic screen shows the execution status, target format, totals, compliant users, candidates, expected updates, failures, duration, candidate account samples, and error details. The final result screen provides the same operational visibility for the real ENFORCE execution, including updated and verified users, pending users, API calls, retries, execution timestamps, and change samples.

Added the manual decision path after the diagnostic so the administrator can choose between Apply Format Now and Finish Without Applying. Corrected the ProcessMaker Visibility Rule configuration for the apply button so that it displays correctly when the diagnostic succeeds and there are users requiring updates.

Improved the action-button presentation by defining dedicated CSS selectors for both manual actions and adding custom CSS to center the buttons, keep consistent sizing and spacing, maintain a clear primary&#x2F;secondary visual hierarchy, and support responsive behavior.

Enhanced the script output so that the Error Sample section no longer appears blank when an execution completes successfully. When no errors are detected, date_format_error_sample_text now returns the message “No se han detectado errores.” instead of an empty value.

Configured the automated path to evaluate the reconciliation result and branch between successful and failed&#x2F;partial executions. The flow includes notification steps for successful reconciliations and reconciliation errors, followed by operational error registration when necessary.

Validated the complete manual flow in the client environment. A diagnostic execution scanned 35 users, identified 33 already compliant and 2 requiring changes, with 0 errors. The subsequent ENFORCE execution updated and verified both identified users successfully, finishing with 0 failures and 0 pending users.

The process is now available in the client environment for additional testing and validation.
